summary.plain: KATRIN measures the mass of the electron antineutrino through precision spectroscopy of tritium beta decay close to its endpoint. From its first five measurement campaigns (259 days) it reports an upper limit of 0.45 electron-volts at 90% confidence level, which tightens its previous bound by a factor of almost two.
summary.technical: Based on the first five KATRIN neutrino-mass measurement campaigns, the best-fit value is m_ν² = −0.14 (+0.13/−0.15) eV², resulting in an upper limit m_ν < 0.45 eV at 90% CL. With six times the statistics of previous data sets (36 million electrons collected in 259 measurement days), a substantial reduction of the background level and improved systematic uncertainties, the result tightens KATRIN's previous bound by a factor of almost two.

title: Direct neutrino-mass measurement based on 259 days of KATRIN data
why_it_matters: The abstract notes that a non-vanishing neutrino rest mass is evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model and that the absolute mass bears importance from particle physics to cosmology. The KATRIN site gives the earlier Mainz and Troitsk upper limit as 2.3 eV/c².
